title: Linear inequalities
log: 2026-11-20T12:15:21Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The closest bank point, Solving linear inequalities, covers solving and the sign flip but not showing the answer on a number line, which the new point requires, and the one-variable card that does include the number line is pitched at Year 8 rather than Years 9 and 10.

draft.title: Linear inequalities
card: An inequality uses \(<\), \(>\), \(\le\) or \(\ge\). Solve it like an equation: do the same to both sides.
Multiplying or dividing both sides by a negative number reverses the sign. For \(-2x < 6\), divide by \(-2\) to get \(x > -3\).
On a number line, an open circle shows \(<\) or \(>\), and a closed circle shows \(\le\) or \(\ge\). The arrow points to the values that work.
Worked example: \(3 - 4x \ge 11\). Subtract 3 to get \(-4x \ge 8\). Divide by \(-4\) and reverse the sign: \(x \le -2\).
draft.remember: Solve as for an equation, but reverse the sign when you multiply or divide by a negative.

a.why: Dividing both sides by \(-3\) gives \(x\) less than \(-4\), and the sign reverses. The option \(x > -4\) forgets to reverse the sign.
a.clue: You divide by a negative number.

b.q: Leo solves \(5 - 2x \le 1\). Which number line description shows his solution?
opts: Closed circle at 2, arrow pointing right
Closed circle at 2, arrow pointing left
Open circle at 2, arrow pointing right
Closed circle at \(-2\), arrow pointing right
b.why: Subtract 5 to get \(-2x \le -4\). Divide by \(-2\) and reverse the sign: \(x \ge 2\). That is a closed circle at 2 with the arrow pointing right. The arrow pointing left comes from not reversing the sign.
b.clue: Divide by \(-2\), then think about which way the sign points.

b.best: Closed circle at 2, arrow pointing right
